content: 1. At higher doses, salicylate levels decrease due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. Close monitoring is required. 2. Calcium carbonate enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergy. This interaction necessitates close monitoring. 3. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of digoxin by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be considered, or administration should be closely monitored. 4. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of diltiazem through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 5. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after medications containing polyvalent cations. 6. Calcium carbonate and doxycycline interact by reducing each other's levels through inhibition of GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be used, or administration should be separated by 2 hours. 7. Drospirenone decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Calcium carbonate reduces eltrombopag levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated. Administration should be separated by at least 4 hours. 9. Calcium carbonate decreases elvitegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy modification or close monitoring is required. Elvitegravir plasma concentrations are reduced when co-administered with antacids due to ionic complex formation in the GI tract, not changes in gastric pH. Doses should be separated by at least 2 hours. 10. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Administration should be separated from antacids by 2 hours. 11. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of enalapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 12. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of ephedrine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 13. Calcium carbonate and erdafitinib interact, and co-administration should be avoided during the initial dosing adjustment period (first 21 days). Serum phosphate levels increase as a pharmacodynamic effect of FGFR inhibition, and phosphate binders may obscure dosage decisions. Alternative drugs should be used. 14. Calcium carbonate increases erythromycin base levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 15. Calcium carbonate increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 16. Calcium carbonate increases erythromycin lactobionate levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 17. Calcium carbonate increases erythromycin stearate levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 18. Calcium carbonate reduces esmolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. 19. Calcium carbonate decreases estramustine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Estramustine should be taken with water at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. 20. Ethacrynic acid decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Calcium carbonate reduces etidronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Administration should be separated by 30 minutes. 22. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of felodipine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 23. Calcium carbonate decreases ferric maltol levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Ferric maltol increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing GI absorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Calcium carbonate decreases ferrous fumarate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Ferrous fumarate increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing GI absorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Calcium carbonate decreases ferrous gluconate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Ferrous gluconate increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing GI absorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Ferrous sulfate increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing GI absorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Calcium carbonate increases flecainide levels by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 28. Fludrocortisone decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Calcium carbonate decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 30. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of fosinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 31. Furosemide decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Calcium carbonate decreases gabapentin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. 33. Calcium carbonate decreases gabapentin enacarbil levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. 34. Calcium carbonate decreases gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Administration should be separated by at least 6 hours. 35. Calcium carbonate and gemifloxacin interact by reducing each other's levels through inhibition of GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Administration should be separated by 2 hours.
